content.text: {"label":"marketing_campaign","explanation":"The general queue started surging right after the 10:50 regional TV spot for the zero-balance savings account (MKT-2026-237, audience 2M, toll-free number on screen). Volume was +53% at 11:15 and +57% at 11:30, and service level fell to 4.8%. The excess is led by new_offer_enquiry (3.71x normal, +53 calls), with spillover into account_update, loan_enquiry and balance_enquiry. AHT is near forecast and staffing is near plan: absences are 3 vs about 2.5 usual. The only open incident is a P4 internal email delay with no customer impact. So this is campaign-driven demand, not an outage or a supply problem. Payments is only slightly over forecast, and its 11:30 service level is 60.3%.","plan_name":"TV-spot surge recovery for general queue","rationale":"General is short by roughly 15-18 agents' worth of work at peak. The plan combines free levers with targeted paid capacity. Breaks and coaching in the next couple of hours are pushed out of the peak. Chat deflection removes up to 20% of new_offer and balance enquiries, the reasons the campaign drives. Callbacks shift peak work to later in the day. A 2-hour overtime offer to 20 agents (about 8 accept, roughly Rs 5,760) covers the core of the spike. A smaller follow-on offer of 10 agents (about 4 accept, roughly Rs 2,880) covers the tail as TV-driven calls decay. Total is about Rs 8,640, well inside the Rs 15,000 budget.
